title: Move NanoBanana to OpenRouter
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
## Summary

- Routes only `nanobanana` through OpenRouter’s exact `google/gemini-2.5-flash-image` endpoint, pinned to `google-vertex/global` with fallback disabled.
- Preserves public name, editing, three references, ratios, seed, paid-only access, multiplier, prices, billing, EXIF, and content-policy 400 responses.
- Restores `gemini-fast` to paid-only access without changing its route or pricing.
- Sanitizes EXIF to public token usage; provider cost and `is_byok` are never embedded.
- No secret change, deployment, fallback, or review request.

## Verification

- Direct generation/edit: 6.1s / 9.2s. Local generation/edit: 5.1s / 7.4s.
- Follow-up paid E2E: valid 1024×1024 JPEG in 7.1s, exact $0.0387051 billing, visually inspected, EXIF inspected with no provider-cost fields.
- `gemini-fast` paid-balance catalog filtering passes; focused Enter aliases/pricing: 285/285.
- Gen: 643/643; both workers type-check.
- CI test setup now injects only a fake in-memory key; no secret is read or changed.

## Accepted product differences

- OpenRouter combines text/reference-image prompt tokens. Total billing is exact because both inputs have the same rate, but the public split is less detailed than Vertex.
- OpenRouter’s image catalog exposes no safety-settings passthrough, so Vertex’s per-request safety thresholds are not preserved. OpenRouter’s own content policy still applies.
